_schema: Room content. The renderer's trust boundary, enforced in room.js:
_plain: PLAIN TEXT, escaped on render: cards[].name, groups[].title, groups[].symbols[].n
_raw: RAW AUTHORED HTML, injected as-is: cards[].body, cards[].note, examples[].q, examples[].steps[], examples[].ans, groups[].symbols[].g
_rule: Anything moved between those two lists changes what the browser does with it. Plain fields must never contain markup; raw fields are trusted and must never hold anything a reader typed.

cards.name: Heat and temperature change
cards.body: q = m·c·ΔT, where ΔT = T<sub>final</sub> − T<sub>initial</sub>
cards.note: c for water = 4.184 J/(g·°C). Positive q = absorbed, negative q = released.

cards.name: Heat is not temperature
cards.body: Temperature measures average kinetic energy; heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference.
cards.note: A bathtub and a cup at the same temperature hold very different amounts of heat.

cards.name: Endothermic vs exothermic
cards.body:
Exothermic: releases heat, ΔH < 0, surroundings warm up.
Endothermic: absorbs heat, ΔH > 0, surroundings cool down.
cards.note: The sign is from the system's point of view, not yours.

cards.name: Enthalpy from formation values
cards.note: An element in its standard state has ΔH°<sub>f</sub> = 0, so those terms drop out.

cards.name: Hess's law
cards.body: Enthalpy is a state function — ΔH depends only on start and end, not the route.
cards.note: Reverse a step ⇒ flip the sign. Double a step ⇒ double its ΔH.

cards.name: Phase changes
cards.body: q = n·ΔH<sub>fus</sub> or n·ΔH<sub>vap</sub>. Water: 6.02 kJ/mol to melt, 40.7 kJ/mol to boil.
cards.note: Temperature holds constant during a phase change, so q = mcΔT does not apply there.

cards.name: Heating curve
cards.body: Sloped where temperature rises (q = mcΔT), flat where a phase changes (q = nΔH).
cards.note: A full heating-curve problem is a sum of both kinds of segment.

cards.name: Calorimetry
cards.body: Heat lost by one thing = heat gained by the other: −q<sub>hot</sub> = q<sub>cold</sub>
cards.note: In a coffee-cup calorimeter the solution absorbs the reaction's heat.

cards.name: Entropy
cards.body: ΔS measures how spread out the energy and matter are.
cards.note: Gas > liquid > solid; more particles means more entropy.

cards.name: Gibbs free energy
cards.body: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS · ΔG = −RT ln K
cards.note: ΔG < 0 ⇒ spontaneous. Temperature decides which term wins.
